name: Malchijah
overview: Malchijah is a male biblical figure noted as a descendant of Harim who had married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:31. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes provided about him. His mention highlights issues related to intermarriage during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchijah means 'YHWH is [my] king,' reflecting a theocentric identity common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of divine kingship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Malchijah as a descendant of Harim, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Malchijah's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returned exiles concerning marriage to foreign women, which was a matter of covenant faithfulness and community purity. His inclusion in the list of those who had married foreign wives underscores the community's struggle to uphold God's commands amid cultural pressures. This account serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to God's covenant in the restoration period.
